newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria March unemployment rises to 14.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria March unemployment rises to 14.5 pct.

text.p: The number of people unemployed in Bulgaria rose to 555,835 or 14.5 percent of the workforce in March from 525,148 in February, a National Labour Exchange (NLE) official said on Wednesday.
"Unemployment rose last month as companies shed employees under a structural reform programme," a NLE spokeswoman told Reuters.
She said further job cuts were inevitable as Bulgaria is to to close down loss-making state firms and reduce red tape under a financial accord with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
Under a memorandum of economic policies agreed with the IMF public sector employment is to be cut by 58,000 positions, with cuts equally divided among the three remaining quarters of 1997.
Some 100,000 employees in industrial firms are also expected to be laid off this year as a result of structural changes, NLE preliminary estimates showed.

The World Bank has approved a $25 million loan for severance payments and compensation for professional retraining, and further $80 million have been earmarked for lending in the course of the reform.
Unemployment peaked in January 1994, when 16.6 percent of the workforce were jobless.

Hit by a severe economic crisis, Bulgaria has earmarked 64 loss-making state enterprises for closure. Restructuring at some of those firms had left some 22,000 people jobless in the last quarter of 1996, NLE figures showed.
Bulgaria's average unemployment rate for 1996 was 11.1 percent, down 0.3 points from 1995.
